topic: The Curious Link: Elastic Collisions and the Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school students interested in physics and computer science

sections.title: The Setup: The Idealized Collision System
lecture_lines: Consider two blocks on a frictionless surface.
Small mass m, large mass M.
Momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.
animations: Show two blocks on surface: small block m (#FF5733) and large block M (#33FF57).
Animate block m moving towards block M with velocity arrow.
Show elastic collision, blocks bounce conserving momentum and energy.
Pulsing glowing circle (#FFFF00) around blocks showing conservation.
Animate block m bouncing off left wall (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Visualizing the Count
lecture_lines: Each collision counts as a hit.
animations: Display digital counter at top left in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate collision; counter increments when block hits wall or block.
Highlight the counter value in yellow (#FFFF00) as digits approach pi.

sections.title: The Geometry of the Solution
animations: Draw velocity vector space with light gray axes (#AAAAAA).
Trace velocity vector as a path in this 2D space.
Animate arc reflecting off boundaries representing collision angles.
